newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen lower after CPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen lower after CPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening lower after the February Consumer Price Index rose 0.3 percent, analysts said. The core rate, excluding food and energy components, rose 0.2 percent.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast a rise, on average, of 0.2 percent in the overall CPI and a 0.2 percent rise in the core rate.
Jim Solloway, director of research at Argus Research
-- "The numbers were a bit worse than consensus, so the gains that we had at the beginning of trading in the bond market have been erased."

-- "That's going to perhaps reduce the optimism regarding the stock market's opening this morning...(The stock market will open) either a little off or not as strongly as had been initially expected."
Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp

-- "If you're going to put a good or bad label, it's bad. But neither label is appropriate. It's not a jolt to the market. On balance, the index came in above expectations, but not so much so that it will scare the markets."
-- "You may have a downward drift to bond prices in early trade, but don't look for anything meaningful."

-- "The data tell you that any upward pressure on wages and benefits has not yet led to an increase in consumer prices. In the current global economic environment it is very difficult for business to raise prices, and that is once again confirmed."
Hildegard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities
-- "The overall number was a little bit higher but the core was in line with expecations. The numbers were met with equanimity. The numbers were in line with forecasts."
-- "The market has been under pressure and will continue to be under pressure ahead of the FOMC meeting next week. We might get a bit of a bounce, but I don't think we're off to the races."
The 30-year Treasury bond was off 2/32 to yield 6.97 percent.
